title: S&P Global Flash Eurozone PMI (Sep 2026) — 08:00 UTC / 04:00 ET, the same-morning European read that sets the tone the US flash lands into
source: EST: THREE primaries, all fetched direct 2026-09-09 by this event's own initial research. (1) S&P Global's forward PMI calendar, pmi.spglobal.com/Public/Release/ReleaseDates?language=en (HTTP 200, 23,858 bytes): 'September 23 ... 08:00 UTC S&P Global Flash Eurozone PMI', inside a same-morning block the same page lists as 07:15 UTC France, 07:30 UTC Germany, 08:00 UTC Eurozone, 08:30 UTC UK, 13:45 UTC US. (2) NEW HERE, and stronger than a forward listing — the publisher's own PAST-RELEASE archive, pmi.spglobal.com/Public/Release/PressReleases?language=en (HTTP 200, 92,883 bytes), records an actually-delivered release at that slot: 'August 21 2026 08:00 UTC | S&P Global Flash Eurozone PMI', with the identical 07:15/07:30/08:00/08:30/13:45 block ordering on that past date. (3) The August release document itself, fetched as a PDF (HTTP 200, 138,214 bytes) and text-extracted in-session, states in its own embargo line: 'Embargoed until 1000 CEST (0800 UTC) 21 August 2026'. 08:00 UTC is 04:00 ET under EDT — five and three-quarter hours before the US cash open and five and three-quarter hours before the US flash. Filed estimate on the standing schema gap, not on date doubt: market-events-data.ts defines no confirmed-source prefix for a private PMI compiler (CAL: is aggregator cross-ref; this is the publisher's own primary), and this lane's hard limits permit a flip only on IR:/BLS:/FED:. Honest asymmetry recorded: the calendar page publishes a release rule for the FINALS only ('Manufacturing PMI: first working day; Services PMI: third working day') and none for the flash, so the flash date rests on the listing and cannot be derived
notes: CANONICAL FILE WRITTEN BY THIS EVENT'S OWN INITIAL RESEARCH (2026-09-09), reading the single prior proposal (…from-sp-global-flash-us-pmi-2026-09-23.json) as input per EVENT-RESEARCH.md. TIER HELD AT low, ON A MEASUREMENT — and holding it is the finding. The proposing ledger filed this entry as the one named, dated, same-morning confound for the US flash's 09:45-10:00 ET window and wrote plainly 'NOT MEASURED: no first-hand bar work was done on the European block; the confound is named, not sized.' Sized here, on the sibling's exact construction so the two are comparable: Yahoo 5-minute bars, range=60d (delivered 2026-06-12..09-08, n=60 sessions), euro proxies FEZ/EZU/VGK/EWG/EWQ against SPY/QQQ/IWM/TLT/^TNX across the three flash days in sample (2026-06-23, 2026-07-24, 2026-08-21). THE CONFOUND IS SMALL. (a) At the US open, the euro-minus-SPY residual — which removes the global factor — ran ABOVE its own median in only 4 of 15 instrument-days against a 50% base rate, so the European complex does not decouple from SPY at 09:30 on these days. (b) In the US flash's own 09:45-10:00 window the sibling's loud finding reproduces on the US five (11 of 14 above median, 6 of 14 at or above p90 against a 10% base) while the EUROPEAN five run 7 of 15 above median and 0 of 15 at p90 — if European risk tone were what makes that window loud, the European-exposed instruments would be loud too, and they are not. (c) The clock runs the wrong way for the confound story: the euro-minus-SPY residual is BELOW base rate at 09:30 (4/15, the window nearest the European print) and above it at 09:45 (14/15, the US slot), so the divergence is created by the US print hours later, not carried in from 04:00 ET. STRUCTURAL FINDING the proposal did not have: the 08:00 UTC Eurozone headline is substantially PRE-ANNOUNCED by its own components — France prints 07:15 and Germany 07:30, and the publisher's own methodology says the Eurozone indices are 'calculated by weighting together the national indices' on Eurostat value-added weights. Both components proposed in this PR. The one place a mark shows is the overnight gap and it is small and surprise-scaled (6 of 15 above median, 1 of 15 at p90; only 07-24 stands out, and the primary-dated 08-21 is the quietest of the three on a 52.1-vs-52.0 nothing print) — recorded MIXED, n=3. FALSIFIER ON THE TIER ITSELF: if on 2026-09-23 the euro-minus-SPY 09:30-09:45 residual ranks ABOVE its own median in 3 or more of FEZ/EZU/VGK/EWG/EWQ, the no-US-hours-footprint null takes its first contradiction and the tier is re-argued rather than patched.
